subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must relate interior angles on one side of a transversal to whether two lines meet
use when parallelism is asserted from the picture instead of from the angle condition
anchor: Two lines cut by a transversal meet on the side where the interior angles sum to less than two right angles, and stay parallel exactly when that sum equals 180 degrees.
ordinary_language_bridge: Compare the two interior angles on one side against 180 degrees, then say which side the lines lean towards.
reconstruction_route: identify the transversal and the two interior angles on one chosen side
conclude meeting on that side, meeting on the other side, or parallel
state the boundary case that separates the two outcomes

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same two lines and the same transversal
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: an interior sum below 180 degrees versus exactly 180 degrees
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: On which side, if either, will the lines eventually meet?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: 180 degrees is the boundary between meeting and remaining parallel

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: lines that look close together in the drawing must meet
misconception_discriminator.probe: supply angle measures that contradict the visual impression of the figure
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner uses the angle sum and overrides the drawing

repair_route: re-mark the interior angles on one side
recompute the sum and compare with the 180-degree boundary
state the conclusion in terms of side of meeting
retry on a figure drawn to mislead
verification_method: repeat the comparison on the other side of the transversal and confirm the conclusions agree
confirm the stated boundary value of 180 degrees is used explicitly
known_limitations: applies to the Euclidean plane and not to non-Euclidean geometries
does not supply the angle measures themselves
